title: CAVIAR: Disentangling Root Causes with an ICA-based VAE for Large-Scale Microservice Systems

problem.claim: Fault diagnosis in large-scale microservice systems is difficult because their heterogeneous metrics are vast, high-dimensional, and diverse.

gap.claim: Existing root cause analysis methods may struggle when only a small subset of metrics drives an observed failure.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes CAVIAR, a two-phase framework for interpretable root cause analysis in large-scale microservice systems.
CAVIAR uses an ICA-enhanced variational autoencoder to learn a low-dimensional, disentangled representation of normal microservice operation.
CAVIAR models faults as external interventions on latent factors, optimizes an interventional matrix to identify a culprit dimension, and maps that factor to original metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Modern microservice architectures produce large quantities of heterogeneous metrics.
Conventional root cause analysis struggles with high-dimensional and diverse metric data.
The authors propose the two-phase CAVIAR framework for interpretable root cause analysis.
The first phase learns a low-dimensional, disentangled representation using an ICA-enhanced variational autoencoder.
The second phase identifies an intervened latent factor and maps it back to original metrics for diagnostics.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, evaluation protocol, or quantitative results are specified.
The abstract does not detail the interventional matrix optimization or how latent factors are mapped to metrics.
The causal validity of treating anomalies as external latent-factor interventions is not established.
